criteria.evidence: All of these pass: preflight_ask, preflight_retry, preflight_dispatch, preflight_planner_round, preflight_critic_round, preflight_run_stage, preflight_resumed_unread_job, preflight_every_stage_error_is_a_budget_short, plus the two not-gated tests for correct and the re-read. The drain entry point is covered by budget_short_dispatch_leaves_the_item_queued_and_the_next_runs. Each test has a held row one cent short and an exact row at the reserve, with the reserves written as literals. The ask, retry, dispatch and resumed tests assert a BudgetShort error and that the next role was not called. The planner, critic and run tests assert a recorded planning stop whose reason says '$0.01 short' and that the next role was not invoked. It passes. planning_and_run_caps_move_by_exactly_the_cap in athena-data passes too. I was not allowed to edit the tree, so I read the tests instead of running a mutated copy. If planning.rs:116 were removed, a second planner call would happen, failing assert planner==1. If planning.rs:336 were removed, a second critic call would happen, failing assert critic==1. If run/mod.rs:1371 were removed, the producer would run, failing assert producer==0.

findings.summary: The newest case in this failure class (the 7th, after the fix landed) had a different cause, and neither the change nor the CHANGELOG says so.
findings.evidence: Evidence snapshot: introspection 20261103-055632-pxgr and job 20261103-055218-kj1t's outcome.json show the planner stopped with error_max_budget_usd after the job had spent $0.87 of a $12.00 job_usd. The planner ran out of its own per-call cap, which the job-budget preflight cannot prevent. It belongs in a separate request, perhaps about planner per-call cap sizing or classification. The CHANGELOG claims the class is fixed but does not say why a case recurred after the fix landed.

findings.summary: For the stage tests, "fails without the change" rests on mutation reasoning, not on reverting the change.

The reading accepted this framing, and reading the tests confirms each would fail if its preflight call were deleted. summary: I recommend this change pass. It does what the accepted reading set out to do. The real fix (`reading::budget_reserve`, the one place the stage caps are added up, plus `Athena::preflight` at each stage) was already in the base: per the evidence snapshot's history.json it landed on 2026-10-30 and 2026-10-31. This change adds tests that prove each entry point checks the budget before it spends. It also adds doc comments and a CHANGELOG entry, and it changes no production logic. I ran every new test and all pass: the 9 `preflight_*` stage tests, the cap table tests in athena-core and athena-data, the syntax-tree scan for a second sum of caps, the CHANGELOG test, and the two drain `budget_short` tests. My grep found only test-code sums of caps, all inside reading.rs `mod tests`. Every changed file is on the deliverables list. I was not allowed to edit the tree, so I could not run a mutated copy. Instead I read each test and checked that it would fail if its preflight call were deleted. Athena's own "fails without the fix" run for criterion 3 passed, as expected: reverting the production files removes only doc comments. So for the stage tests, "fails without the change" rests on that reading, not on a revert. One thing the change does not say: the newest case in this failure class (job 20261103-055218-kj1t, after the fix landed) was not a job-budget problem. The planner ran out of its own per-call cap after the job had spent about $0.87 of $12.00, so it was filed under the wrong class.
